# Mohammad Hamza

> Mohammad Hamza is a Senior Frontend Engineer based in India, with 6+ years of experience building e-commerce platforms, Web3 applications, ERP interfaces and interactive web experiences. He works with React, Next.js, TypeScript, Shopify (Online Store 2.0, Functions, Checkout Extensions, custom apps), ERPNext/Frappe, Solana and EVM wallets, and Three.js with GLSL. He works remotely as a freelance Frontend & ERP Developer.

## Quick facts

- Role: Senior Frontend Engineer; currently Frontend & ERP Developer (Freelance)
- Location: India
- Experience: 6+ years (since 2020)
- Education: Bachelor of Computer Science, CSJM University, Kanpur, 2020
- Recognition: Awarded “Promising Newcomer” at ITH Technologies for quickly ramping up on complex Web3 systems and delivering high-impact frontend solutions.
- Focus: React, Next.js, Three.js / WebGL, Shopify, Web3
- Website: https://www.erhamza.tech/

## Profile

Results-driven Frontend Engineer with 6+ years of experience building e-commerce platforms, Web3 applications, ERP interfaces and interactive web experiences. Proficient in React, Next.js, TypeScript and Shopify, with deep expertise in Shopify Store 2.0, Shopify Functions, Shopify Extensions and custom app development.

Strong focus on performance optimization (SSR/SSG and code splitting, 30–50% gains), scalable architectures, reusable components, REST/GraphQL API integration, offline-first apps and conversion-driven UI/UX.

Adapts quickly to new domains (Web3, Shopify, 3D web), with strong problem-solving and self-learning capabilities. Currently learning backend development (Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL).

## NAVIG

- Category: Interactive web
- Status: live
- Year: 2026
- Engagement: Freelance client project

- Stack: React, Three.js, GLSL, GSAP

A visually rich website for a crypto and AI intelligence product. As you scroll, a 3D scene of 25,000+ glowing particles reshapes itself into ocean waves, waterfalls and data streams, and it runs at 144 frames per second.

## CodesLytic Budget

- Category: Full-stack and Product
- Status: live
- Year: 2026
- Engagement: Built for a client
- Role: Built end to end by me as the sole developer, for a client
- Stack: Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, IndexedDB, Playwright, Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS EC2
- Tools used: Claude Code
- Link: https://app.codeslytic.com
- Page: https://www.erhamza.tech/projects/codeslytic-budget

A budgeting app that keeps working without internet and syncs when you are back online. It tracks money in many currencies, repeats monthly bills on its own, and splits shared expenses between friends, including paying each other back through UPI.

### Highlights

- Accounts, nested categories, multi-currency tracking, monthly budgets with alerts and projections, recurring transactions on a background worker (time zones, DST, month-end safe)
- Splitwise-style group expenses (equal, exact, percentage, share) with exact-sum rounding, debt simplification, settlements and UPI settle-up
- Offline-first sync engine (IndexedDB, idempotent outbox, field-level merge, conflict inbox) and an installable PWA with WCAG 2.2 work
- Money stored as integer minor units with a shared TypeScript domain core; rotating refresh tokens, Argon2, CSRF checks and multi-tenant access control (per-user data isolation)
- GitHub Actions CI/CD with Docker deploy to AWS EC2 and automatic rollback

### Results

- 1,500+ unit/integration and 160+ E2E test cases (owner-reported)

## Trading Desk and Multi-sig

- Category: Web3
- Status: private (not linked)
- Year: 2024
- Engagement: Employer: ITH Technologies
- Role: Frontend developer in a team. Built DEX & CEX trading dashboards with real-time data and wallet integrations; integrated Solana exchanges (Raydium SDK, SPL tokens, RPCs). Developed a multi-signature wallet with secure transaction workflows; worked with Node.js backend services and APIs alongside the frontend.
- Stack: React, Next.js, Ethers.js, Wagmi, Web3.js, Solana RPC, Raydium SDK
- Link: none
- Page: https://www.erhamza.tech/projects/dex-cex-multisig-wallet

Live trading screens for crypto exchanges that show prices as they change, and a multi-signature smart-contract wallet in the style of Safe (formerly Gnosis Safe) that requires approvals from a set minimum number of owners (such as 2 of 3) before any transaction runs. It removes single points of failure for individuals, teams and DAOs managing digital assets on Ethereum and compatible chains.

### Highlights

- Proposal, confirm and execute flows
- Wallet tagging and recovery
- Governance dashboards

## NFT Marketplace

- Category: Web3
- Status: shut down (no longer online)
- Year: 2024
- Engagement: Employer: ITH Technologies
- Role: Main frontend developer, leading the blockchain integration of the smart contracts. The contracts were written by others.
- Stack: React, Paymaster, Solana Web3, ERC-721, ERC-1155
- Link: none
- Page: https://www.erhamza.tech/projects/nft-marketplace

A marketplace, similar to OpenSea, where creators make, buy and sell digital collectibles. It used ERC-721 and ERC-1155 contracts on Base, with Sui and Solana supported alongside. It had minting and trading flows, lazy minting (listing an item before it is minted), auctions and fixed-price sales, and creator dashboards, and the platform covered the network fee when creators minted. I was the main frontend developer and led the blockchain integration of the smart contracts, which were written by others. The project has since shut down.

### Highlights

- Marketplace supporting ERC-721 and ERC-1155 with minting and trading flows
- Lazy minting, auctions and creator dashboards

## ERPNext for Manufacturing

- Category: Full-stack and Product
- Status: private (not linked)
- Year: 2026
- Engagement: Client; in daily use at the factory
- Role: Sole developer. Mapped the client’s manual production workflow, then built a custom frontend app to replace it using native backend APIs and functions.
- Stack: ERPNext, Frappe, Next.js, Docker, GitHub Actions
- Link: none
- Page: https://www.erhamza.tech/projects/erpnext-manufacturing

A custom app built on ERPNext that replaced a factory’s manual production tracking by reproducing the existing workflow. It records what goes into each product, the work orders and how much each worker made, then creates the weekly payment vouchers for labourers. It is in daily use at the factory.

### Highlights

- Custom doctypes and workflows for BOM, work orders and production tracking
- Payment voucher generation for weekly completed quantities for labourers
- Docker-based ERPNext environment with GitHub Actions CI/CD
